overview: This form of Mahito counts hits on each target to trigger an extra attack. Its unique settings tune that counter and the third normal attack.
technicalOverview: Instant Spirit Body of Distorted Killing (CP_250) is a cursed-spirit record without a Character Select entry whose character data selects UCP_250_ActionController and a CP_250-specific AI think node, not AGameShikigami or ShikigamiUniqueDataTable. Its CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterUnique list contributes two populated CharacterUniqueDataTable2 rows. Row 0 (CP_250) is the passive hit-counter setup: a 7.0-second reset window and hit requirements of 5, 4, and 3 at cursed-energy levels 1, 2, and 3. Reaching the level's count clears that receiver's counter and queues a CP_250_PASSIVE multi-hit request. Row 1 (CP_250_ATTACKE) tunes the custom NormalAttack_3/AttackE chain: a 1.0-second first wait, a 5.0-second guard-sensitive final wait, and a 1.0 multiplier on cursed-energy exp from qualifying hyper-armor damage. CP_250's many custom attack subclasses also add surface-dependent impacts and inherited CN_090 super-attack slots, but those traced effects use hard-coded values, animation events, or data-table IDs rather than these unique floats. Indices 4-13 of row 0 and 3-13 of row 1 are zero and have no identified reader in the traced sources; zero alone is not proof that a slot is unused.

CP_250.title: Passive hit counter and reset timer
CP_250.overview: This row controls the CP_250 passive that counts landed hits on each receiver. A hit is ignored while cursed-energy disable time remains or when the receiver index is the 0xFF sentinel. Otherwise the per-receiver count increases, a level-specific threshold may convert it into a CP_250_PASSIVE request, and any counted hit at level 1-3 restarts the reset timer. The timer only counts down while input is enabled; when it expires, all receiver counts are cleared.

0.label: Passive count reset time
0.simple: How long landed hits stay counted toward the passive before the counter is forgotten.
0.technical: The stored value is 7.0. In UCP_250_ActionController::AddPassiveHit, after the CursedEnergyDisabledTimeLeft <= 0.0f and PlayerIndex != 0xFF gates and after the switch has accepted CursedEnergyLevel 1, 2, or 3, HitCountResetTimer is assigned GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(0, 0). This happens whether or not the hit reached the threshold. UCP_250_ActionController::ActionTick only decrements it while the timer is > 0.0f and the owner's input data reports input enabled; the decrement is DeltaTime / Dilation, where Dilation is CustomTimeDilation when that is > 0.0f and 1.0f otherwise. Once the timer is <= 0.0f, HitCounts.Reset() clears every receiver. Units are seconds because the code accumulates DeltaTime. Two generic, non-CP_250-specific readers also use (0, 0): SteerTowardSecondaryTarget requires it to be > 0.0f and divides an angle by it, and ProjectionSorceryReceive uses it as a fallback restraint time only when Request.DamageTableRow is null; no CP_250 source calls either path.

1.label: Level 1 passive hit threshold
1.simple: At cursed energy level 1, five counted hits trigger the passive.
1.technical: Read only in the case CursedEnergyLevel == 1 of UCP_250_ActionController::AddPassiveHit. After HitCounts[PlayerIndex] is incremented, the code tests HitCounts[PlayerIndex] >= static_cast<int32>(GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(1, 0)). On success it removes that receiver entry, finds the character by EGameCharacterIndex(PlayerIndex), and, if found, queues one AddMultiHit request using damage row CP_250_PASSIVE. The switch default returns before the threshold or timer assignment, so levels outside 1-3 count the hit but do not trigger or restart anything. The stored value is 5.0; a higher value requires more counted hits, a lower value requires fewer.

2.label: Level 2 passive hit threshold
2.simple: At cursed energy level 2, four counted hits trigger the passive.
2.technical: Read only in the case CursedEnergyLevel == 2 of UCP_250_ActionController::AddPassiveHit. It replaces the level-1 divisor in the same flow: compare the incremented per-receiver HitCounts value against static_cast<int32>(GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(2, 0)), then clear that receiver's count and queue CP_250_PASSIVE if the target lookup succeeds. The stored value is 4.0; higher values need more hits and lower values need fewer. No other CP_250 reader for (2, 0) was identified.

3.label: Level 3 passive hit threshold
3.simple: At cursed energy level 3, three counted hits trigger the passive.
3.technical: Read only in the case CursedEnergyLevel == 3 of UCP_250_ActionController::AddPassiveHit. The incremented per-receiver HitCounts value is compared with static_cast<int32>(GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(3, 0)); on reaching it, the count is removed and the same CP_250_PASSIVE AddMultiHit request path runs. The stored value is 3.0; higher values need more hits and lower values need fewer. The controller's cached CursedEnergyLevel is initialized to 1 and normally follows the clamped status level; values outside 1-3 use the switch default and skip this slot.

notes.text: Guarded hits count too: slot 210 calls AddPassiveHit when a guarded hit's receiver is a character, that character's slot-179 flag is true, and the owner is the instigator; slot 212 applies the same count to dealt damage. CP_250's slot 160 identifies CP_250_PASSIVE as a passive damage row.

The separate CP_250_Passive buff status uses its own BuffDebuff row floats: FloatValue[1] adds to the cursed-energy exp rate and FloatValue[0] adds to the attack rate. Those are not FloatValues from this CharacterUnique row, even though the names are similar.

CP_250's slot 183 uses the shared full-gauge cursed-technique check at 0x141052E60 rather than the base max-level check, and slot 205 uses the shared CN_090/CP_020 homing-warp effect body. Neither body reads a unique float.

CP_250_ATTACKE.title: Normal Attack 3 / AttackE timing and reward
CP_250_ATTACKE.overview: This row is reached by the CP_250-specific NormalAttack_3 and NormalAttackAir_3 action templates only. In a chained start (action start count 0), it gates two timed phases of the AttackE follow-up decision. It also scales the cursed-energy exp awarded to the owner when hyper armor absorbs ordinary damage. The row name matches the AttackE attack-set family, but the runtime finds it by its zero-based Id_CharacterUnique position, row 1.

0.label: First AttackE follow-up wait
0.simple: How long the chained normal attack waits before it can choose a follow-up.
0.technical: TCP_250_NormalAttack_3<TBase>::TickAttack reads GetOwnerUniqueFloat(0, 1) only when the action's start count is 0 and Phase is 0. Each tick first adds DeltaTime to ActionElapsedTime, then returns while 1.0 > ActionElapsedTime; the stored value is 1.0 seconds. At exactly 1.0 or later the branch proceeds to normal-attack button and left-stick checks. Increasing this value delays the first decision point; decreasing it makes the decision earlier. At a start count of 1 the base TickAttack runs instead and this slot is not read.

1.label: Guard-sensitive final AttackE wait
1.simple: Without Guard held, the chain waits up to five seconds before parking; holding Guard skips that wait.
1.technical: This is read later in the same start-count-0, Phase-0 branch, after the earlier button/stick alternatives have not returned. TCP_250_NormalAttack_3<TBase>::TickAttack returns while GetOwnerUniqueFloat(1, 1) = 5.0 > ActionElapsedTime and IsGameKeyHeld(EGameInputKey::Guard) is false. At exactly 5.0 or later, or immediately while Guard is held, it sets NextAttackType to the 0xFF sentinel, plays AttackE_01_02, and increments Phase. FilterRequests later requests the chosen follow-up (NormalAttack_1, NormalAttack_2, or NormalAttack_2_1) only when Byte16 is 1; a pending unrelated NormalAttack_3 request is removed when NextAttackType is not NormalAttack_3. Higher values lengthen this no-Guard wait; lower values shorten it. Units are seconds because ActionElapsedTime accumulates DeltaTime.

2.label: Hyper-armor hit exp multiplier
2.simple: Scales the cursed-energy exp gained when hyper armor lets certain hits land.
2.technical: TCP_250_NormalAttack_3<TBase>::OnDamageReceived first returns unless bHyperArmorNotifyActive != 0 and DamageRow->AttackType is neither SuperCursedEnergyAttack nor SpecialTagCombo. It computes Ratio = Damage / HitPointMax; only when Ratio > 0.0f does Exp become GetLastLevelThreshold() * Ratio, where GetLastLevelThreshold returns CursedEnergyRow->LevelThreshold[3]. It then calls AddCursedEnergyExp(GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(2, 1) * Exp). With the stored 1.0 the amount is unchanged; larger values increase the awarded exp and smaller values reduce it. If Ratio <= 0, Exp stays 0 and the multiplier has no effect. AddCursedEnergyExp itself returns for a defeated owner or zero exp. A non-hyper-armor-ignoring damage row also plays SE_CP_250_02001, which is independent of this multiplier.

notes.text: The same template is instantiated for CreateAction cases NormalAttack_3 and NormalAttackAir_3, so row 1's three reads apply to both grounded and aerial third normal attacks. The air class only overrides the attack-set lookup.

CP_250's CursedEnergyAttack_1 chooses its impact by animation UniqueAction IntParameter 0-3 and by the map-ground row under the effect; it does not use row 1 values. The air variant returns false from ShouldSpawnGroundEffect, while the ground variant creates surface FX and a tracked decal for impact 1.
The SuperCursedEnergyAttack subclasses inherit CN_090's slots 70, 130, and 132 and add only a surface-effect UniqueAction; none of those inherited or overridden slots reads a unique float.

Row indices are zero-based positions in CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterUnique. AGameCharacter builds UniqueRows in that order and GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue is an unchecked UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] dereference; FGameCharacterAction::GetOwnerUniqueFloat and its inline variant are only forwarding helpers. CP_250's readers use literal row 0 or 1, not a dynamic row-index helper.

Character setup switches to UCP_250_ActionController and FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CP_250. The AI node's own setup and tick manage behavior weights, level bands, and a SuperCursedEnergyAttack state sentinel; those paths contain no unique-float access.

No CP_250-specific .inl file exists in the traced source tree. The only relevant inline helper is the generic FGameCharacterAction::GetOwnerUniqueFloatInline; MakeUniqueCameraRequest is also generic but CP_250 action code never calls it, so none of the zero camera-style slots in either row can be assigned a camera use here.

Do not import CN_250's dynamic GetLevelRowIndex/GetUniqueRow reads or its trap/spawner forwarding into CP_250. CP_250's controller is a direct UGameCharacterActionController subclass; its CreateAction override maps only its own normal, cursed-energy, and super attack action types, and its shared slots do not forward into trap unique-float access.

UCP_250 post-processing is animation/sequencer state only (rotate alpha and tail/cloth rotators); it has no unique-row read. The sequencer module toggles the same SetSequencerRotateAlphaEnabled body shared with other post-process anim instances.
